name: /wtft
tagline: Where The F***ing Tokens?! (WTFT) - Cost Auditing Widget
description: Displays a horizontal, stacked TUI bar chart widget of your session's cost during each activity (Spec, Code, Plan, Agents, ...). Bars are cost totals tagged by each turn's action - every turn's cost includes the context re-send overhead regardless of category, and Prompt means pure conversational replies. For an input/output token decomposition use --tokens.

why.scenario: You just finished a coding session and want to see where your token costs went — was it all spec-writing or code refactoring?
why.result: A stacked bar chart widget appears showing your cost during each activity (Spec, Code, Plan, Agents, ...) over 1-hour intervals. You see exactly which hours cost the most.

why.scenario: You're tracking costs over a full workday and want finer granularity.
why.result: The last 12 four-hour intervals are displayed, giving you a two-day cost breakdown at quarter-day resolution.

why.scenario: You're auditing Claude Code sessions (not Pi) to compare costs across harnesses.
why.result: The chart pulls session data from your Claude Code session directory instead of Pi's, rendering the same bar chart for Claude interactions. (CLI only — the Pi extension auto-discovers Pi sessions.)

why.scenario: You want to scroll through a long cost history that doesn't fit in the TUI widget.
why.result: A fullscreen scrollable pager overlay opens with the expanded cost timeline. (Pi TUI only — not available in the CLI.)

why.scenario: The 'Other' category in your WTFT widget is consuming a large share of your session cost and you want to drill into which specific commands are causing it.
why.result: A grouped histogram appears, breaking 'Other' commands into semantic sub-categories (Build & Bundling, Linting & Formatting, System Utilities, etc.) with per-command counts and costs. Unclassified commands appear under their own section.

why.scenario: You're running Claude Code and want a companion terminal showing live token costs as your session progresses.
why.result: A real-time updating bar chart renders in-place as new interactions are logged. Runs until Ctrl+C or 'q'. Scrollback above the chart is preserved. Ideal in a separate tmux pane.

why.scenario: You want to see the exact USD amount on your billing invoice or reconcile costs across multiple providers.
why.result: WTFT uses public pricing estimates per model and excludes things like caching discounts, free-tier credits, or provider-specific billing nuances. It's a directional cost-awareness tool — not an accounting ledger.

why.scenario: Your session has been idle for a while and the model cache has expired, or you're running a local model like Ollama with no remote caching at all.
why.result: Instead of hiding the widget or showing stale data, WTFT displays 'Cache Empty' (cloud models) or 'No Cache (local model)' in the widget area, plus the daemon's idle countdown. You know immediately whether the session is just idle or cache-free.

usage.desc: Group cost data into arbitrary binned intervals of minutes, hours, days, or weeks (e.g., 1m, 7m, 4h, 1d, 2w; default: 1h).
Limit the number of interval bars displayed (default: 10).

Specify an explicit session .jsonl file path, or a fuzzy substring filter (e.g. 'b04c'). When the argument is not an existing file, it filters discovered sessions by basename or path substring. If exactly one match, runs immediately; if multiple, shows the session selector filtered to matching sessions.
Working directory for Claude Code session discovery (default: current directory).
Set the maximum character width of the TUI widget (default: 240).
Set the display timezone (e.g., America/New_York, Europe/London, Asia/Tokyo) to avoid UTC display on servers (default: system local).
Render mode. --cumulative (default) shows running sums over time; --bucket shows discrete interval cost buckets.
Enable (default) or disable the proportional cost scale tick marks above the bars.
Launch an interactive scrollable fullscreen pager overlay to view expanded cost history.
Print a histogram of 'Other' commands grouped by semantic sub-category (Build, Lint, Test, System, etc.) with per-command counts and costs.
Show (default) or hide the WTFT cost-auditing widget below the editor.
Enable or disable emoji icons in TUI widgets. When disabled, clean single-width ASCII characters are used instead.
Watch a session file for changes and re-render the bar chart in real-time (companion terminal mode for Claude Code). Ctrl+C to exit.
List all running log parsers with session path, PID, parser version, and idle time.
Kill log parsers whose source session no longer exists.
Kill all running log parsers (fresh spawn on next wtft).
Stop log parser for a specific session path.
Kill the log parser, delete tag files, and force a full session re-parse.
Target a specific harness for auto-discovery (pi, claude-code, or auto). Default: auto.
Thinking token budget for utilization percentage display in --tokens output.
Switch between token-unit mode and cost-unit mode ($). --tokens shows a per-model token summary table with utilization. --cost switches back to $ mode. Config-persistable.
Pad output with N spaces on each side (default: 1, max: floor(term/2)-1). Makes CLI output width match Pi TUI widget.
Print diagnostic cost totals (tag file vs direct parse + dedup) after the chart.
Display this help information.
Display this tool's version.
Explain why you'd run this tool, with user scenarios and anti-use-cases.

Group token costs into custom 7-minute intervals.
Render binned date/time labels in Eastern Standard Time.
Show last 20 4-hour interval bars of cumulative token costs.
Force show or refresh the cost audit widget.
View a full, scrollable cost audit timeline inside a fullscreen TUI pager.
Print a histogram of 'Other' commands grouped by semantic sub-category.
Hide the cost audit widget from the display.
Print a per-model token summary table to cross-reference costs with /usage.
Watch a session file in real-time and re-render the bar chart as new interactions arrive.
Print diagnostic cost totals (tag file vs direct parse + dedup) after the chart.
Render with zero padding (full terminal width). Default --pad 1 matches Pi widget width.
